_comment: The look, in one place. Every stage reads this; nothing hardcodes a look value any more.
This is the SHIPPED look. The app opens on it and renders through its own copies, passed as
LOOK_FILE, so it never edits this file; change the shipped look by hand — it is just numbers.
tone.* are the arguments to scripts/make-tone-lut.py. luts/tone/shipped.cube is GENERATED
from them. Freshness is by CONTENT, not mtime: the cube stamps its parameters into its TITLE
and ensure_tone_lut (scripts/lib.sh) regenerates it whenever those disagree with this file,
so the .cube can never silently disagree with the numbers recorded here.
correct.* is the input-correction stage, which runs BEFORE Apple's conversion and therefore
in log: exposure and white balance in linear (decoded and re-encoded with Apple's published
transfer function), then an ASC CDL — slope, offset, power, which is what lift, gamma and gain
wheels are. At the values below it does NOTHING, and a neutral correction leaves the filter
out of the graph rather than rendering every pixel through a lookup that returns it.
look.lut names the film-emulation cube by its stem in luts/looks/, or "none" for no look at
all. It lives here rather than in a script because it is a look value, and because the tone
block below was tuned WITH this cube in the chain: the two belong to each other.
Provenance of the current values: graded by eye in the Bench (since retired)
against the RAL references in frame, then adjusted once for shadow detail (black 0.015 ->
saturation 1.27 is DELIBERATELY off-spec — it puts the traffic blue at B/G 2.39 against a
1.98 spec. That is the grade, not an error.
match.reference_yavg is the post-CST luma mean (10-bit) the look was tuned against, measured
on IMG_0609. grade.sh solves each clip's gamma to land on it, so that every clip in a shoot
window gets the same look rather than the same curve. It lives here because it is a
measurement of the grade, not a knob: change it only if the look is re-tuned on another frame.
